clue.text: Bestselling author recalls explosives expert

definitions.meaning: the pen name of the American writer of the Wheel of Time fantasy series
the American dynamiter sent to blow a bridge in Hemingway's For Whom the Bell Tolls

explanation.surface: A popular novelist's memoir looks back on a bomb-disposal specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalls' is a link: the novelist's pen name brings to mind Hemingway's hero, who shares it.
explanation.definitionFit: One name belongs both to a fantasy novelist writing under a pseudonym and to Hemingway's bridge-blowing Spanish Civil War volunteer.

clue.text: Lady, neighbour of Anne Elliot, capable of persuasion

definitions.text: Lady, neighbour of Anne Elliot, capable of persuasion

parts.words: Lady, neighbour of Anne Elliot, capable of persuasion
parts.note: in Jane Austen's Persuasion the heroine's titled neighbour and godmother talks her out of her engagement to Wentworth

explanation.surface: A titled woman living near Austen's heroine is good at talking people round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capable of persuasion' describes the character and names the novel she appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's Persuasion gives Anne Elliot an older friend, a baronet's widow nearby, whose advice persuades Anne to break off her engagement.

clue.text: Potter's featureless pigling

definitions.meaning: Beatrix Potter wrote The Tale of Pigling ___, about a young pig
featureless means dull, lacking anything distinctive

explanation.surface: A Potter piglet with no distinguishing characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the full name of Beatrix Potter's pig, and the middle word alone defines his surname as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and characterless things are described by this adjective, which Beatrix Potter also gave as a surname to her pig hero.

clue.text: "The Idler is always inquisitive and seldom 7 " (Samuel Johnson)

definitions.text: "The Idler is always inquisitive and seldom 7 " (Samuel Johnson)

parts.words: "The Idler is always inquisitive and seldom 7 " (Samuel Johnson)
parts.note: a quotation from Johnson with its last word missing; the solver supplies the adjective meaning able to hold on to what is learnt

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 7 stands where the missing word belongs in Johnson's sentence; the idler asks questions but keeps little of the answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's sentence contrasts curiosity with a memory that keeps hold of things, the sense of the missing adjective.

clue.text: Cooper's knave starts with row

parts.note: Its title starts with a word for a knave and goes on with a word for a row

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker's rascal kicks off a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooper' looks like a barrel-maker and 'row' like a quarrel, but the cooper is James Fenimore Cooper and 'row' is a tier, so his novel's title opens with the knave of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave in a pack of cards is also called by this name, the first word of Cooper's title before Tier.

clue.text: Poet in terrible riot about return of a Durberville

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
terrible signals that the letters of riot are badly thrown about

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: return of means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the most famous Durberville

explanation.surface: A poet caught up in an awful disturbance over a Hardy heroine's homecoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Durberville' points to Hardy's heroine Tess, whose family claimed d'Urberville descent; 'return of' reverses her name and 'about' wraps the shuffled riot around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel and Christina, siblings of the Pre-Raphaelite circle, were both noted poets with this surname.

clue.text: Unfinished merchant ship in Agamemnon's city

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for the ship loses its last letter

parts.note: an argosy is a large merchant ship

explanation.surface: A half-built trading vessel lies in the Greek king's port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the final Y off ARGOSY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Agamemnon ruled from Mycenae and the city in the Argolid that gave the region its name, so it is often called his city.

clue.text: Maugham's island with somewhat firmer association with

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Maugham's island with somewhat firmer association with', ends on a dangling 'with': its cross-reference (probably to 14, flying) is missing and no reprint found
annotationWithheld.clue: Maugham's island with somewhat firmer association with

clue.text: Task that may be a bit of an imposition

definitions.meaning: task here means a set piece of work, especially schoolwork

definitions.text: that may be a bit of an imposition
definitions.meaning: an imposition is a punishment exercise set at school, so a set piece of it fits

explanation.surface: A chore that is rather an unwelcome burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of an imposition' reads as 'rather a nuisance', but an imposition is a set punishment exercise at school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived word means a set lesson or punishment exercise given to a pupil.

clue.text: Fast fighter identified by copper Greek city's sheltering

indicators.note: sheltering means the city's name gives cover to the metal's symbol inside it

parts.note: Sparta was the warlike Greek city; the 's gives the S
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A quick soldier is recognised by a policeman sheltering in a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like 'quick' but is Howard Fast, whose novel tells of the gladiator; 'copper' is the metal, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Fast wrote the novel about the Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Accent on Marvell's fine and private place?

definitions.meaning: an accent mark sloping down from left to right over a vowel
Andrew Marvell's To His Coy Mistress says the tomb is a fine and private place, where none embrace

explanation.surface: A stress mark on a poet's favourite secluded spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'The ___'s a fine and private place, / But none, I think, do there embrace' from To His Coy Mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a backward-sloping accent mark and the burial place Marvell calls fine and private.

clue.text: Amis put up with it, finally

definitions.text: Amis put up with it, finally

parts.words: Amis put up with it, finally
parts.note: Kingsley Amis's novel is titled with this word followed by Up; put 'up' with it and you have the title, and the word itself means a close

explanation.surface: In the end the novelist tolerated it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' reads as 'tolerated', but means add 'up': Kingsley Amis wrote the novel Ending Up. 'finally' points to the word's sense of a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion or close is what comes finally, and it forms the first word of Amis's novel title.

clue.text: Fewer paths to follow to Bennett's Hilda

parts.note: fewer means less
paths are ways

explanation.surface: Fewer routes lead to Arnold Bennett's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' says the surname comes after 'Hilda': Hilda Lessways is the second of Arnold Bennett's Clayhanger novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Bennett's novel Hilda Lessways names its heroine; her surname is what follows 'Hilda'.

clue.text: Unexpected denial of Introduction

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of denial turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A surprising refusal to be introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage that leads a listener into a story or broadcast is an introduction.

clue.text: Common ground for Johns and Audubon?

definitions.text: Common ground for Johns and Audubon?

parts.words: Common ground for Johns and Audubon?
parts.note: W. E. Johns wrote the Biggles flying stories and Audubon painted the birds of America; both deal with flight

explanation.surface: Two writers share a common interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is paradoxical: what the two share is the air, Captain W. E. Johns with his pilot Biggles and John James Audubon with his birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the air, by aircraft or by bird, is the shared subject of Biggles stories and Audubon's paintings.

clue.text: It affected J. B. Morton's Doctor of Utrecht?

definitions.text: It affected J. B. Morton's Doctor of Utrecht?

parts.words: It affected J. B. Morton's Doctor of Utrecht?
parts.note: J. B. Morton, as Beachcomber, invented Dr ... (Whom God Preserve) of Utrecht, whose name means a squint

explanation.surface: An illness strikes a comic writer's Dutch doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachcomber's mad inventor Dr Strabismus is named after the eye condition, so the condition 'affected' him in name.
explanation.definitionFit: A squint, eyes that do not line up, is the medical condition whose Latin form gave Beachcomber's doctor his name.

clue.text: New avatar aim in ancient Buddhist monument

indicators.note: new means the letters of avatar and aim are made up afresh

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fresh incarnation's goal lies in an old Buddhist site.
explanation.definitionFit: The great stupa in Andhra Pradesh, built around the third century BC, is a famed early Buddhist site.

clue.text: Heard lad in Swiss speech

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Heard lad in Swiss speech', gives no wordplay for ROMANSCH: only 'Swiss speech' defines and 'Heard lad' yields none of its letters; it may be an OCR echo of 18-down

clue.text: Greek playwright addressed in bible?

definitions.meaning: a writer of Athenian New Comedy, rival of Menander
Paul's short New Testament epistle is addressed to this Colossian Christian

explanation.surface: A Greek dramatist is spoken to in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a comic dramatist of ancient Athens and to the man Paul wrote to in a New Testament letter.

clue.text: Heard bird in basic speech?

indicators.note: heard means the word for the bird is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a pigeon is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird is overheard using rudimentary language.
explanation.definitionFit: A simplified contact language mixing words from two tongues is basic speech.

clue.text: Sailor king of 6

definitions.meaning: in some accounts this hero sailed with Jason as one of the Argonauts
he ruled Argos, the answer to 6-down, and was father of Adrastus

explanation.surface: A seaman who rules a Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth makes this figure both an Argonaut on Jason's voyage and king of Argos, father of Adrastus.

clue.text: General view of Liddell Hart

parts.note: the military historian Basil Liddell Hart wrote a biography of the Union general who marched through Georgia

explanation.surface: An overall opinion held by a military historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General view' reads as 'overall opinion', but it is the American Civil War general Liddell Hart studied in his book Sherman: Soldier, Realist, American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union general of the March to the Sea is the subject of Liddell Hart's 1929 biography.

clue.text: Wagner's has a fragile association with

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Wagner's has a fragile association with', ends on a dangling 'with': its cross-reference (probably to 14, flying) is missing and no reprint found

clue.text: His London audience may have had a surprise

definitions.text: His London audience may have had a surprise

parts.words: His London audience may have had a surprise
parts.note: the composer wrote his twelve London symphonies for concerts there, one nicknamed the Surprise for its sudden loud chord

explanation.surface: A performer's audience in London got an unexpected shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Surprise Symphony (No 94), one of the London symphonies, has a sudden fortissimo chord in its quiet slow movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote the Surprise Symphony for his London concerts of the 1790s.

clue.text: Show off Cocteau ballet

definitions.meaning: to show off is to display ostentatiously, to strut
Cocteau wrote the scenario of the 1917 Ballets Russes work with music by Satie and designs by Picasso

explanation.surface: Flaunt a French ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt ostentatiously is the verb; the 1917 Satie-Picasso ballet devised by Cocteau has the same title.

clue.text: Excuse for Tami Hoag's man …

definitions.meaning: an excuse claiming one was elsewhere
Tami Hoag wrote the thriller The ... Man

explanation.surface: A pretext offered for a novelist's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; the word is both an excuse and the first word of Hoag's title, The ___ Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that one was somewhere else is an excuse, and Hoag's suspect is the man who has one.

clue.text: … her man is also partly Patrick Leigh Fermor subject

indicators.note: partly means only a part of the words her man is is used

explanation.surface: Her man also is in part what a travel writer wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'herMAN IS'; 'also' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leigh Fermor's travel book of 1958 is about the remote middle peninsula of the southern Peloponnese.

clue.text: Associate of films merchant offers Forster adaptations

definitions.text: Associate of films merchant offers Forster adaptations

parts.words: Associate of films merchant offers Forster adaptations
parts.note: the producer Ismail Merchant's partner directed the films of A Room with a View, Maurice and Howards End

explanation.surface: A film trader's colleague puts forward screen versions of Forster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merchant' is not a trader but the producer Ismail Merchant, whose partner James directed their Forster films.
explanation.definitionFit: The director James, Ismail Merchant's lifelong partner, made the celebrated Forster film adaptations.

clue.text: Spurious sort of man is producing sorcery

parts.note: spurious means sham, fake

indicators.note: sort of suggests a kind of version of the letters of man is, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fake type of man produces magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns MANIS into ANISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing and spirit contact through a tribal priest is a form of magic, so sorcery fits.

clue.text: I end in heroic version of Epictetus manual

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: I finish in an epic translation of the Stoic's handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek title of Arrian's handbook of Epictetus's Stoic teaching means a little manual held in the hand.
